answer: An agent economy can require every identity to post a refundable stake before it may submit jobs, then slash that stake when a randomly audited job fails a verifiable result check. Audits sample across accounts, while repeated failures tied to the same funding source or behavior can trigger a larger bond requirement, without treating shared infrastructure alone as proof of fraud. A Sybil attacker must therefore lock real capital in each account and risks losing it; creating identities is no longer free. The onyx, lagoon, and oasis queues can all apply the same rule.
